correctness.rationale: In characteristic five shifting by X_5 changes the power sums only by lower power sums, so on the sum-zero hyperplane the equations are independent of X_5. The directional coordinate multiset contains zero, and Newton identities give T^5+e_4T. Nonzero direction implies e_4≠0; the polynomial is separable and its roots are a scaled copy of F_5. The 120 arrangements modulo affine relabeling give six rational geometric points. Finiteness here excludes a common curve component before applying Bézout: six distinct points exhaust intersection length six. The homogeneous complete intersection is saturated (depth one), giving the reduced affine cone and hence the reduced projective lines. The polar matrix for p_2 after elimination is 2(I+J) in dimension three, of determinant 2 modulo five. Thus the preserved conic is smooth, has six rational points, and S_5 acts faithfully on them because the order-twenty stabilizer contains no nontrivial normal subgroup of S_5. Comparing order 120 with Aut_F5(conic) gives the claimed action. In the complete-local normalization, homogeneous terms embed by branch evaluation. The (2,3) Hilbert series has ranks 1,3,5,6,…; comparing to six coefficients at every degree gives delta 9. At degrees at least three every branch coordinate is available, while no degree-two form can isolate one point since that would vanish at five points of a smooth conic without containing the conic. Isolation at lower degree would imply isolation at degree two by multiplication by a suitable linear form. This proves the exact branch conductor orders. Normalization separates the six lines, and adding their point counts with the common rational vertex counted once gives 6q+1 and the claimed zeta function. An independent bounded F_5 check corroborated the polar determinant, six directions, evaluation ranks and action order; it is not a geometric exhaustion over the algebraic closure. The frozen checker was inspected, not run.

evidence: The prior exact model explicitly gives D=V(Q,P), Q=a²+b²+c²+ab+ac+bc, with all six direction points rational, and the S_5 action with Sylow-five normalizer stabilizer. It gives the normalized local ring and the conductor in it, and proves the lines meet only at the rational vertex.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The displayed Q is smooth since its polar matrix is I+J with determinant 4 modulo five; all six rational directions therefore exhaust its rational points. The conic is preserved by coordinate permutations since Q comes from the invariant quadratic form, and the already specified faithful Sylow action has order 120, equal to PGL_2(F_5). Thus the conic realization adds no nonmechanical invariant. Counting six known split lines with one common rational point gives 6q+1 and its zeta function directly. The normalization and exponent-three formulation are already explicit in the earlier proof.

value.rationale: The degeneration and singularity of this natural model are worthwhile but already resolved in the earlier exact-model record. The residual additions are an elementary conic realization of the already determined six-point action and the point count and zeta function of the already determined split line arrangement. Neither closes a further scientific gap in the frozen claim; the alternative root-polynomial proof is not a new result. No corrected remainder is proposed.
